items.title: Document service and secure object storage flows
acceptanceCriteria: Direct-upload intents validate the declared document class, content type and size before a signed upload URL is issued; finalization validates the stored object's actual size and magic-number content type before metadata registration, DOCUMENT_UPLOADED publication, or clean-download eligibility
Tenant-scoped signed access and document metadata are audited

evidence.note: The first criterion was corrected on acceptance because it contradicted the approved architecture it was meant to describe. ADR-014 has the client PUT straight to private object storage, so bytes reach storage before this platform can read them: no validation of "real content type" can precede that by construction. What the platform actually guarantees is two checks at two moments — declared class, type and size before a credential is issued, and the stored object's actual size and magic-number type before it is registered, announced or downloadable. No scope or estimate changed; COM-004 remains 13 points.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service exec jest --selectProjects integration -t 'what the bytes actually are'
evidence.note: The corrected criterion, proven on real bytes in real storage: an HTML page uploaded as a PDF, an executable whatever it is called, a real file of the wrong type for its class, an empty object and a finalize with nothing uploaded are all refused. The declared/detected mismatch is reported as a mismatch rather than silently corrected, and the size persisted is the one storage reports.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service exec jest --selectProjects integration -t 'what the boundary refuses'
evidence.note: The pre-credential half: an unknown document class, a content type the class does not permit and a declared size over the class limit are each refused before any upload URL exists, and an unknown field is refused rather than dropped.

The second criterion: another organization's document is reported absent rather than forbidden, receives no download URL and cannot be deleted; listings are scoped; the oversight role and roles with no document business are refused outright. Every state change is recorded — DOCUMENT_UPLOADED, DOCUMENT_SCANNED, DOCUMENT_DELETED and VIRUS_DETECTED carry the actor and correlation id through the transactional outbox, and deletion is a tombstone the database refuses to accept without an actor, time and reason.

userStory.asA: tenant user who is permitted to attach evidence
userStory.iWant: a short-lived URL for a direct upload to private object storage
userStory.soThat: large files never pass through the application service or its database

acceptanceCriteria.given: an authenticated tenant user declares an allowed document class, content type and size
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user requests an upload URL
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service creates a tenant-scoped intent with a server-generated opaque key and returns a bounded short-lived signed PUT URL

acceptanceCriteria.given: the request is unauthenticated, outside policy or attempts to supply an object key
acceptanceCriteria.then: the request is refused without creating an intent or exposing storage credentials

evidence.note: Scaffolds the service with a tenant-scoped UploadIntent, an S3 storage port and a server-generated opaque object key. The client never supplies or influences the storage path; src/storage/object-key.ts derives it, and the documents bucket is private with no anonymous policy.
Binds the signed PUT URL to the declared Content-Type so the signature genuinely covers it. Before this fix the type was advisory and a URL issued for one type could be replayed for another.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'the signed URLs themselves'
evidence.note: storage-and-outbox.int-spec.ts against a real MinIO: 'signs an upload URL to one content type, so it cannot be reused for another', 'refuses a URL whose expiry has passed' and 'never puts the secret key in the URL'. The URL is bounded, short-lived and genuinely type-bound.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'redeeming an upload intent'
evidence.note: document-lifecycle.int-spec.ts: 'writes an object key the client never chose', 'cannot be redeemed by another organization' and 'refuses an expired intent and records the expiry'. Key substitution and cross-tenant redemption are both refused.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'what the boundary refuses'
evidence.note: api-document.int-spec.ts: 'refuses an unknown document class', 'refuses a content type the class does not permit' and 'refuses an unknown field rather than dropping it'. The companion case 'refuses a declared size the class does not permit, before issuing anything' proves an out-of-policy request creates no intent.

object-key.spec.ts proves the object key is server-generated and opaque, carrying no caller-supplied path segment, and dto.spec.ts proves the request schema has no field a client could supply one through. 273 unit tests pass on the merged implementation.

E2E scenario 'carries the file to storage without it passing through the platform': the bytes travel straight from the client to MinIO over the signed URL, so the file never transits document-service or PostgreSQL. 'refuses an unauthenticated caller and the oversight role' covers the closed-by-default path. 10/10 green on 2026-08-31.
Pull request carrying the implementation; the reviewable diff for this story.
PR #16 is the second implementation pull request for this service. It did not change the intent path, and its integration suites re-prove it unchanged against the merged composition.

stories.title: Finalize and validate a directly uploaded object

userStory.asA: tenant user who completed a direct upload
userStory.iWant: the platform to verify and register the uploaded object
userStory.soThat: document metadata refers only to the expected file and its real content

acceptanceCriteria.given: the expected object was uploaded for an active intent
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service verifies object ownership, size and magic-number content type, persists tenant-scoped metadata and publishes DOCUMENT_UPLOADED through the transactional outbox

acceptanceCriteria.given: the object is missing, empty, oversized, expired, substituted or has a declared and detected type mismatch
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service refuses registration and does not publish a successful upload fact

evidence.note: Adds finalization with magic-number content inspection (src/content/magic-number.ts, src/content/policy.ts), object-existence and intent-ownership verification, tenant-scoped metadata persistence, and an outbox row written inside the same transaction as the document.
Exercises the HTTP surface through the real Nest application rather than a hand-built harness, so finalization is proven through the composition a deployment actually gets.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'what the bytes actually are'
evidence.note: document-lifecycle.int-spec.ts against real PostgreSQL and real MinIO: 'refuses an HTML page uploaded as a PDF', 'refuses an executable whatever it is called', 'refuses a real file of the wrong type for its class', 'refuses an empty object' and 'refuses to finalize when nothing was uploaded at all'. Declared-versus-detected MIME mismatch and empty objects are refused on real content, not on the client's word.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'issues a URL, accepts a real upload, and registers what was actually stored'
evidence.note: The happy path verifies the object exists and persists tenant-scoped metadata. 'returns the size storage actually holds, not what anyone declared' in storage-and-outbox.int-spec.ts proves the size is read back from the bucket rather than trusted from the request.

api-document.int-spec.ts: 'returns the same document rather than creating a second' and 'writes the outbox row inside the same transaction as the document'. DOCUMENT_UPLOADED is transactional, and 'publishes the upload event exactly once across a replay' proves no duplicate fact.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'cannot be redeemed by another organization'
evidence.note: Object-key substitution and cross-tenant intent redemption are refused, so a rejected finalization never publishes a successful upload event.

E2E 'publishes DOCUMENT_UPLOADED carrying the honest scan state' reads the real Kafka topic, and 'refuses content that is not what the client declared' proves the mismatch refusal end to end through the gateway.
Pull request carrying the implementation; the reviewable diff for this story.

PR #16 moved scanning out of finalization: a document is now registered PENDING and DOCUMENT_UPLOADED carries that state. Object verification, magic-number detection and the single-transaction outbox write are unchanged, and are re-proven by the same integration suites.

stories.title: Authorize safe document metadata and download access

userStory.asA: user authorized for a specific document
userStory.iWant: to read its metadata and obtain a short-lived download URL when it is clean
userStory.soThat: private evidence is available without weakening tenant or object-level access

acceptanceCriteria.given: a clean active document and an authorized caller in its tenant
acceptanceCriteria.when: metadata or a download URL is requested
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service returns only authorized metadata or a bounded signed GET URL for that object

acceptanceCriteria.given: a cross-tenant caller or a pending, not-scanned, infected, quarantined or deleted document
acceptanceCriteria.when: metadata or download access is requested
acceptanceCriteria.then: object-level authorization and the fail-closed scan policy refuse access without revealing storage details

evidence.note: Makes download fail-closed: only a genuine CLEAN verdict authorizes a signed GET URL. src/document/download-policy.ts refuses PENDING, NOT_SCANNED, INFECTED, FAILED, QUARANTINED and DELETED, and storage is never asked to sign a URL for a refused state.
Corrects the OpenAPI document so the download-URL endpoint publishes the HTTP success status it actually returns, instead of one it never emits.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'the application a deployment gets today'
evidence.note: api-document.int-spec.ts on the production composition, which is now ClamAV: 'composes ClamAV, which inspects content' reads the bound scanner off the booted AppModule, 'says plainly that nothing has examined the content yet' covers the PENDING window a document is registered in, and 'refuses the download, because no scan has cleared it' returns HTTP 422 while leaking nothing about storage. Superseded the earlier stub-based assertions, which described a composition this service no longer ships.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'when a download is refused'
evidence.note: document-lifecycle.int-spec.ts: 'refuses while the scan is pending, and issues no URL at all', 'refuses an infected document', 'refuses a deleted document as absent', 'refuses a document nothing inspected - which is every document in MVP' and 'issues no signed URL at all when it refuses'. Every non-CLEAN state is fail-closed.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'when a scanner has cleared the document'
evidence.note: With the test-only AlwaysCleanScanner: 'issues a signed URL that returns the exact bytes' - the downloaded bytes match the upload exactly - plus 'serves it as an attachment, never as something a browser renders' and 'refuses once the document is deleted, and calls it absent'.

Cross-tenant and object-level authorization: 'reports another organization document as absent, not forbidden', 'does not issue a download URL to another organization', 'does not let another organization delete it', 'lists only the caller organization documents', 'refuses the oversight role outright', 'refuses a role with no business handling documents' and 'is not callable by another service at all, valid token or not'.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'the events this service publishes'
evidence.note: 'never publishes VIRUS_DETECTED from a scanner that inspects nothing' and 'publishes VIRUS_DETECTED when an engine that really inspected content finds one'. The infected fact is emitted only for a genuine result from a content-inspecting provider.

Q-18 is CLOSED (2026-08-31) by ADR-049: self-hosted ClamAV, pinned to an immutable digest, bound behind the same MalwareScanner port. The production composition inspects content, so a CLEAN verdict is reachable and this story's first criterion — a bounded signed GET URL for a clean document — is satisfiable for the first time. NOT_SCANNED is retained only as the honest record of rows written while the question was open, and is still refused. AlwaysCleanScanner and fake-clamd live under test/, which tsconfig excludes from the build.

Answers Q-18 at the composition root: a real ClamAV behind the existing MALWARE_SCANNER port, so a document can be cleared for download for the first time. There is one path to CLEAN and it requires all of a reply that parsed, as OK, from an engine whose version was read, on a signature database inside the freshness window. Timeout, refused connection, malformed reply, engine error, oversize object, a scan that stopped at a limit and a stale database are all FAILED with a reason code.

Adds the quarantine record as a property of the row rather than a promise in a document. ck_document_infected_is_quarantined refuses an INFECTED row with no quarantine, so there is no instant in which a document is known infected and undecided about - not even through a hand-written UPDATE.

Fixes a fail-open defect the tests found: openReadStream asked storage for exactly maxBytes, so a larger object returned exactly the ceiling, the byte counter never tripped, and the scanner read a truncated prefix and reported OK about a file it had only seen the start of. It now asks for one byte past the ceiling, which makes 'there is more than we allow' observable.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service exec jest --selectProjects integration -t 'the EICAR test artefact'
evidence.note: clamav-scan.int-spec.ts against a real ClamAV, real PostgreSQL and real MinIO: 'is detected by the engine, from bytes that reached storage over a signed URL', 'is quarantined in the same write as the verdict, never after it', 'stays non-downloadable, and is refused without revealing storage', 'keeps the object as evidence rather than destroying it' and 'publishes VIRUS_DETECTED exactly once, carrying the signature and no bytes'. EICAR is assembled in memory from two base64 fragments and never written to the host filesystem.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service exec jest --selectProjects integration -t 'a file the engine finds nothing in'
evidence.note: The clean path end to end: a document is registered PENDING and refused, then becomes CLEAN attributed to the engine and signature database that cleared it, then receives a bounded signed URL whose bytes match the upload exactly and which is served as an attachment. This path was unreachable before ADR-049 - nothing ever issued a CLEAN verdict.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service exec jest --selectProjects integration -t 'when the scanner is unavailable'
evidence.note: Fail-closed proven rather than described: with the scanner unreachable the document stays PENDING and undownloadable, the failure is visible through readiness and telemetry with a reason code and no address, and once the retry budget is spent it becomes FAILED - still refused, and still attributable to an engine that never answered.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service exec jest --selectProjects integration -t 'what a pending or infected document reveals'
evidence.note: 'shows no object key, bucket, endpoint or credential in its metadata' and 'issues no signed URL at all when it refuses' - the second spies on the storage port and fails if a URL is created and then discarded, because a credential that existed is a credential that existed.

protocol.spec.ts enumerates nine malformed clamd replies - truncated, unterminated, two messages on one connection, a signature named Doc.Dropper.OK-Agent - and proves none parses as CLEAN. transitions.spec.ts enumerates every allowed and forbidden state transition and proves no failure reason the port defines can reach CLEAN. env.spec.ts proves a production deployment refuses an unauthenticated TCP scanner and exits. 255 unit tests pass.

11/11 green on 2026-08-31 against the running stack with a real ClamAV: 'is scanned by a real engine, and becomes downloadable only then' polls the asynchronous verdict through the gateway, and 'hands back the exact bytes once the scan has cleared it' completes the capability ADR-014 has described since day one.

Q-18 is closed with the implemented decision, the image source and pinned digest, the FreshClam mechanism, the resource cost and the replacement path - and with an explicit statement of what ClamAV does not give: a CLEAN means 'nothing this database knows about matched', not 'safe'. No claim of complete or guaranteed detection appears anywhere.

stories.title: Delete a document without erasing its audit trail

userStory.asA: tenant user authorized to remove a document
userStory.iWant: to delete it with an explicit reason
userStory.soThat: access ends while the platform retains factual audit evidence

acceptanceCriteria.given: an active tenant-owned document and an authorized caller with a reason
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service records the actor, reason and time, prevents further download and publishes DOCUMENT_DELETED through the transactional outbox

acceptanceCriteria.given: the same authorized deletion is retried
acceptanceCriteria.then: no second domain effect or contradictory audit fact is produced

evidence.note: Fixes the API Gateway so a DELETE request body is forwarded downstream instead of being silently dropped. Without it the caller's stated deletion reason never reached document-service.
Reads the includeDeleted query flag as written, so a tombstone is excluded from the default listing while the record itself is retained.
proxy.service.spec.ts regression tests protecting the fix: 'forwards a DELETE body when the caller sent one' and 'sends no body on a DELETE that had none' - a plain DELETE stays a plain DELETE.

document-lifecycle.int-spec.ts: 'records who, when and why rather than erasing the row' (actor, reason and timestamp), 'removes the object from storage', 'is idempotent, and does not overwrite the original actor or reason', 'publishes exactly one deletion event across repeated calls' and 'excludes a deleted document from the default listing'. DOCUMENT_DELETED goes through the transactional outbox and a repeat produces no second domain effect.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'refuses a deletion with no stated reason'
evidence.note: api-document.int-spec.ts refuses a deletion that states no reason, 'refuses once the document is deleted, and calls it absent' proves it is no longer downloadable, and 'does not let another organization delete it' holds the tenant boundary on the destructive path.
ck_document_deleted_has_actor is one of the seven invariant-carrying CHECK constraints verified through up to down to up: a deletion with no recorded actor cannot exist at the database level.

E2E through the real gateway: 'records a deletion as a tombstone and reports it as absent afterwards' and 'excludes the tombstone from the default listing but keeps the record'. This exercises the DELETE-body forwarding fix end to end.
Pull request carrying the implementation; the reviewable diff for this story.

PR #16 did not change the deletion path. Its integration suites re-prove the tombstone, the single DOCUMENT_DELETED fact and the idempotent repeat against the merged composition, and the ck_document_deleted_has_actor invariant is re-verified by the migration reversibility harness across both migrations.

stories.title: Operate and verify the Document Service boundary

userStory.iWant: the Document Service, private object storage and gateway route to be observable and repeatably deployable
userStory.soThat: document flows can be operated and verified without hidden infrastructure steps

acceptanceCriteria.given: the documented local or CI environment is started
acceptanceCriteria.when: health, migration and end-to-end document checks run
acceptanceCriteria.then: PostgreSQL, private MinIO buckets, gateway routing, service telemetry and the direct-upload lifecycle are reproducible with no real secrets

acceptanceCriteria.given: the implementation is proposed for merge
acceptanceCriteria.when: repository quality and security gates run
acceptanceCriteria.then: reversible migrations, meaningful branch coverage, API and event contracts, image build and required security scans pass

evidence.note: Gives the CI pipeline a private MinIO bucket with deterministic setup, a dedicated PostgreSQL database and the coverage gate, so the document jobs run against real infrastructure rather than mocks.

Puts the service on the coverage gate documented in docs/14 section 14.2 - 75% statements, branches, functions and lines - measured across both the unit and integration projects, with collectCoverageFrom anchored at the package root so no domain file is silently excluded.

Scopes the twenty-per-hour document upload cap (docs/06 section 6.9) to unsafe methods only, so listing and reading metadata run on the platform default and one screen of documents cannot lock a user out for an hour.
Adds the document-api Playwright project proving the direct-upload lifecycle against a running stack: Keycloak, api-gateway, document-service, PostgreSQL, MinIO and Kafka.
Adds a boolean environment parser that reads "false" correctly, so a flag explicitly disabled in configuration is not silently treated as enabled.

402 tests across 18 suites (273 unit, 129 integration) against real PostgreSQL, real MinIO and a real ClamAV. The authoritative CI measurement in main run 33484616100 and PR #17 run 33491369897 is 90.15% statements, 82.07% branches, 88.28% functions and 91.77% lines against the documented 75% gate on all four, unchanged. collectCoverageFrom stays anchored at the package root, so no domain file is excluded.

Reversible migration proven up to down to up against a throwaway schema: the four tables (upload_intent, document, access_grant, outbox_message) and seven critical invariant-carrying CHECK constraints are present, gone, and back. The migration defines 10 named domain ck_* CHECK constraints in total; the harness verifies the seven that carry the invariants.

rate-limit-scope.spec.ts: the upload cap 'applies to a write', 'applies to a deletion', 'does not apply to a read' and 'does not apply to a HEAD or an OPTIONS either'. Reads do not consume the upload budget.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service run test:integration -- -t 'the probes an orchestrator uses'
evidence.note: Health and readiness against the real database: liveness without a token, readiness, the startup probe, a build identifier carrying no business data, metrics exposed for scraping, and 'leaves the probes reachable without a token, and nothing else'.

Full E2E suite green: 73/73 across economic-api, marketplace-api and document-api against the running stack, the document project contributing 9 scenarios including a real ClamAV scan and a byte-for-byte download. The count moved from 74 to 73 because two added scenarios were folded into the uploads that already existed rather than performing their own — the gateway caps document writes at twenty per hour (docs/06 § 6.9), and a suite that needed that relaxed would be testing something the platform does not do.

CI run 33390350065 on merge commit d257fb3 (PR #14): success. The four pull-request jobs were green. The image build and Trivy scan is main-only by pipeline design and was skipped there; it has since executed on main for this service — see the merge-run evidence below.
Operability and delivery evidence is recorded under the version-2 governance model; the service earns no Story Points until the product owner accepts it.

Provisions the pinned ClamAV image in the integration and E2E jobs over a Unix socket - the production transport, so CI proves what a deployment uses rather than only what a laptop can reach. freshclam is off in both for determinism; that updating works is proven by a separate clamav-signatures job that runs it for real against the mirrors.

Adds the ClamAV and freshclam services to docker-compose with a persistent signature volume, a non-root read-only container and a loopback-only port. Also moves fake-clamd.ts out of src/: under this tsconfig it would have been compiled into dist and shipped inside the production image.

Fixes a tenant-guard misconfiguration found while reading the service: TENANT_SCOPED_MODELS named marketplace-service's models, so the guard scoped nothing. No cross-tenant read was reachable through it - the explicit checks covered every path - but the layer A-04 asks for was inert. tenant-scope.spec.ts now derives the expected set from schema.prisma so it cannot drift again.

The coverage gate ran on every pull-request revision and on merged main, rising from 88.70/79.75/84.56/90.00 at PR #14 to the authoritative CI measurement of 90.15/82.07/88.28/91.77 in main run 33484616100 and PR #17 run 33491369897, against a 75% gate that was never moved.

up to down to up in 33.2s across both migrations, with a data-rollback probe the empty-schema reversal cannot make: the init schema permitted an INFECTED document with no quarantine record, so the forward migration is applied over a seeded one and asserted to carry it through quarantined rather than aborting halfway. Twelve invariant-carrying CHECK constraints verified present, gone, and back.

evidence.ref: pnpm run ci:image-matrix && pnpm run test:image-matrix
evidence.note: The eight-service image matrix is unchanged and its guard passes with all four negative controls. ClamAV is an external sidecar dependency, not a ninth Rasta service, so it is scanned by its own CI job rather than added to a matrix derived from services/*/Dockerfile.

0 CRITICAL/HIGH findings against the pinned digest, scanned locally on 2026-08-31 before making the gate blocking. The CI job uses the same severity and the same exit-code 1 as every Rasta image - the threshold is not relaxed because the image is somebody else's.

freshclam verified live with persistent signature storage: the named volume was seeded from the pinned image at daily-28108 and freshclam updated it to 28109 incrementally, rather than re-downloading ~110 MB. clamd runs as uid 100 with a read-only rootfs and answers clamdscan --ping.

Readiness distinguishes scanner health from storage and database health, reporting engine version, signature version, signature age and freshness separately, plus downloadsRequireCleanScan so an operator reading the probe during an incident does not have to know canDownload's rule to see that nothing has opened up. A scanner outage is a degraded entry, not a 503 - uploads, metadata and deletion still work and downloads are already fail-closed.

75/75 E2E green on 2026-08-31 against the running stack, up from 74 - the added scenario is the byte-for-byte download after a real scan. Five marketplace failures on a first attempt were a Temporal gRPC transport limitation of Docker Desktop on this Windows host, not a repository defect; with Temporal started the way CI starts it, the whole suite is green.

Operational runbook for the three alert conditions, whose first section is 'nothing has opened up': a scanner outage makes new documents unavailable, never available. Includes the backfill SQL for documents that FAILED during an outage, with an explicit warning never to include INFECTED or NOT_SCANNED in it.
Pull request carrying the implementation; the reviewable diff for this story.

Second implementation pull request, merged 2026-09-01. PR #14 delivered the service; PR #16 delivered the scanner that made its download path reachable, and is the reviewable diff for everything ClamAV-related.

Merge commit on main with exactly two parents — 3b4df26 (previous main) and 928710e (PR #16 head) — created with a normal merge commit rather than a squash or rebase, so the eleven implementation commits remain individually reviewable. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 928710e origin/main` confirms the head is an ancestor of main.

Main CI run 33484616100 on 4464e95: success, 13/13 jobs. Lint/types/unit, Security scans (Gitleaks no leaks, pnpm audit at high clean, Semgrep 156 rules over 569 files with 0 findings), ClamAV image scan and signature freshness, Integration and security tests, End-to-end 73/73, and Build and scan images for all eight Rasta services. This is the first main run in which the image matrix executed with the scanner in the tree.

All eight Rasta service images built and Trivy-scanned on main: identity, organization, asset, fleet, maintenance, economic, marketplace and document. Every job ran both a Build image and a Scan image step at CRITICAL/HIGH with exit-code 1 and ignore-unfixed, so a pass is a scan that found nothing rather than one that was skipped. document-service reported 0 vulnerabilities.

The ClamAV dependency has its own gate, because the eight-image matrix is derived from services/*/Dockerfile and an external sidecar would otherwise be the one container we deploy that nobody scanned. It Trivy-scans the pinned digest at the same CRITICAL/HIGH threshold, records the engine and signature versions the pin carries (ClamAV 1.5.4, main-63, daily-28108, bytecode-339), and proves freshclam genuinely updates — it reached the mirrors and moved daily to 28110. Kept separate from the deterministic suites, which run with freshclam off on purpose.

Both migrations reversed up to down to up against a throwaway schema, including a data-rollback probe the empty-schema reversal cannot make: an INFECTED document with no quarantine record — which the init schema permitted — is seeded, the forward migration is applied over it, and it is asserted to come through quarantined rather than aborting halfway. Twelve invariant-carrying CHECK constraints verified present, gone and back.
